sovereign_country.strategic_role: 支持全中文章程、传统华人客群离岸家族信托常驻地

meta_jurisdiction_context.jurisdiction_name_en: Samoa (unitary national jurisdiction; no sub-state corporate registry or sub-national tax distinction)
meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Hybrid — English Common Law tradition codified by local statute (including the International Companies Act 1987 model), with Samoan customary law applicable to land and chiefly titles; a unitary jurisdiction for corporate and tax purposes.
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Agreement between the Government of the Independent State of Samoa and the Government of the People's Republic of China on the Reciprocal Promotion and Protection of Investments (Samoa-China BIT, in force since 1999)
Pacific Agreement on Closer Economic Relations Plus (PACER Plus) — comprehensive trade and economic cooperation treaty in force for Samoa
Pacific Island Countries Trade Agreement (PICTA) — preferential trade agreement among Pacific Islands Forum members, in force for Samoa
Agreement Establishing the World Trade Organization (Samoa has been a WTO Member since 10 May 2012)

Bilateral Tax Information Exchange Agreements (TIEAs) with Australia, New Zealand and other OECD member states — active bilateral tax-cooperation treaties; Samoa currently maintains no comprehensive double taxation agreement in force

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Money Laundering Prevention Act 2007 (No. 22 of 2007), as amended (MLPA 2007), together with the Financial Intelligence Unit Guidelines issued thereunder; International Companies Act 1987, as amended, including the International Companies Amendment Act 2018 (beneficial ownership and economic substance); International Companies (Economic Substance) Rules 2019; International Companies (Fees) Regulations; AML/CFT directions and licensing conditions of the Samoa International Finance Authority (SIFA) applicable to registered agents; and FATF Recommendations as adopted through Samoa's membership of the Asia/Pacific Group on Money Laundering (APG).
ubo_and_aml_profiling.ubo_disclosure_level: Government_Only_Access — the UBO register is maintained by the licensed Samoan registered agent and is accessible to the Registrar of International Companies, SIFA, the Samoa Financial Intelligence Unit and domestic/foreign competent authorities on lawful request; it is not part of the publicly searchable company register.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified copy of passport (or national photographic ID) of each proposed director, shareholder and ultimate beneficial owner
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Passport/ID issuing authority of the holder's country; attestation by a qualified notary public
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (or consular legalization where the issuing state is not an Apostille Contracting Party)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank reference letter and source-of-funds/source-of-wealth confirmation for each ultimate beneficial owner
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Issuing licensed bank or regulated financial institution
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (or consular legalization), with bank seal and authorized signatory attestation

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incorporation, Certificate of Good Standing, and register of directors and shareholders of any corporate shareholder (where a UBO is corporate)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Home-jurisdiction companies registry (or the Registrar of International Companies, Samoa, if the corporate shareholder is a Samoan entity)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized board resolution and power of attorney authorizing the Samoan registered agent and incorporation counsel
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary public of the corporate shareholder's home jurisdiction

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Beneficial Ownership Declaration and corporate KYC/AML questionnaire (statutory UBO register form)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: SIFA-licensed Samoan registered agent / designated compliance officer
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Internal statutory record maintained by the registered agent; no external apostille required

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Professional introducer reference letter (licensed attorney, accountant, or regulated trust-company officer)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory pre-incorporation and ongoing screening of all directors, shareholders, ultimate beneficial owners and authorized signatories against: (i) the Samoa FIU PEP database and domestic gazetted terrorism lists; (ii) the UN Security Council Consolidated Sanctions List; (iii) the US OFAC SDN List and consolidated sanctions list; (iv) the EU Consolidated Sanctions List; and (v) adverse-media and integrity checks under MLPA 2007 and FATF Recommendations 1, 10, 12, 22 and 25. Enhanced Due Diligence (EDD) is mandatory for any PEP, family member or close associate, and source-of-wealth and source-of-funds evidence must be obtained wherever a UBO holds 25% or more of the company, is politically exposed, or is connected to a sanctioned jurisdiction. Any screening match must be escalated immediately to the designated Money Laundering Reporting Officer and the Samoa FIU within statutory timelines; no incorporation may proceed until the match is lawfully resolved.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Samoa International Companies Registry — Name Clearance / Name Reservation Facility of the Registrar of International Companies, Ministry of Commerce, Industry and Labour (MCIL), coordinated with the Samoa International Finance Authority (SIFA); official portal www.mcil.gov.ws and www.sifa.ws.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The company name must be expressed in Roman/Latin script, may be in the English or Samoan language, and must end with 'Limited' or 'Ltd.'. A name in a non-Roman script (including Chinese, which is common for the traditional Chinese-family trust client segment) is accepted only with the prior written approval of the Registrar and must be accompanied by a certified transliteration and English translation; the Registrar may additionally require a statutory declaration explaining the meaning, pronunciation and phonetic equivalence of the transliterated name before clearance is granted.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Samoa (where used in a manner implying connection with the Samoan Government or otherwise misleading)
International (where implying intergovernmental or sovereign status)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon rejection, the Registrar issues a written statement of reasons. The applicant may (i) file an amended name-reservation application within 14 days of the rejection notice, (ii) request one extension of an existing reservation for a further 30-day term by paying the prescribed extension fee before the initial window expires, and (iii) if still aggrieved, lodge a formal written appeal with the Minister of Commerce, Industry and Labour within 14 days of the rejection notice, with a further right of judicial review before the Supreme Court of Samoa where the ministerial decision remains adverse. The appeal must annex the original clearance application, the Registrar's written reasons, a corrected name proposal, and evidence of payment of the appeal filing fee.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Not permissible as a substitute: every International Company must maintain a physical registered office in Samoa through a SIFA-licensed registered agent, and a virtual office cannot satisfy this statutory requirement. For a deep-sea RoRo (ISIC 5012) vessel-owning entity, the International Companies (Economic Substance) Rules 2019 further require genuine decision-making presence in Samoa — local board/management meetings, locally retained corporate records, adequate premises, and qualified staff — such that a merely administrative virtual address carries a high risk of challenge by SIFA, the FIU and the Registrar.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Moderate-to-high for an active shipping International Company: estimated 40–60% probability of an unannounced or short-notice on-site inspection and records call by SIFA or the Samoa FIU within the first 12 months of operation, rising above 65% where economic substance is outsourced, exemptions are invoked, or UBO documentation is incomplete.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Name search and name reservation application fee (single proposed name)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Registrar of International Companies, Ministry of Commerce, Industry and Labour (MCIL)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Statutory incorporation fee and issuance of the Certificate of Incorporation
Licensed registered agent and registered office service — first year, including statutory register keeping and filings
UBO register setup, AML/KYC file preparation and customer due diligence (ownership-tree analysis, source-of-funds intake, CDD verification)
Notarization, authentication and consular legalization or Hague Apostille of the UBO/corporate document bundle
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Notary public and Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Trade (or issuing-state competent authority)

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: International Companies Act 1987 (Samoa), ss. 6-16 (Incorporation, Memorandum and Articles) and s. 95 (Tax Exemption); International Companies Regulations 1998
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registrar of International Companies, Samoa International Financial Services Authority (SIFSA)
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Memorandum and Articles of Association (statutory Form IC-1 and IC-10 accompanying documents)
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No minimum paid-up capital requirement; shares may be denominated in any currency; no escrow account required
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED THAT: (1) the share subscriptions set out in the Register of Members are hereby approved and allotted; (2) the registered office of the Company shall be situated at [Registered Agent Address], Apia, Samoa, or as subsequently resolved; (3) [Name] and [Name] are appointed President and Secretary-Treasurer, respectively, to hold office until removed by ordinary resolution; (4) the President and Secretary-Treasurer, acting jointly, are authorised to open bank accounts, execute contracts and sign any vessel acquisition or charter documentation; and (5) this resolution shall be effective immediately and superintendent.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registrar of International Companies via SIFSA licensed registered agent; SIFSA counter, Apia or online
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the prescribed name reservation request together with the proposed name, business scope declaration and proof of registered agent engagement. Pay the reservation fee and obtain the name approval certificate.
required_dossiers: Copy of registered agent engagement letter
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is identical or misleading, file a fresh application with a distinctive alternative name; appeal any refusal to the Registrar within 14 days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Draft and Notarize Memorandum and Articles of Association
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Samoa-qualified legal counsel; overseen by SIFSA Registrar
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the Memorandum and Articles of Association in compliance with the International Companies Act 1987, including capital structure, share classes, director powers and permitted business of deep-sea Ro-Ro vehicle transport. Ensure execution and notarization by a duly authorized notary public.
required_dossiers: Notarized consent of each founding director
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registrar returns the documents for non-compliance, amend the offending clauses and resubmit through the registered agent within five business days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the signed and notarized Memorandum and Articles, statutory officer consents and certified identification copies through the SIFSA online portal or in person. Pay the prescribed incorporation fee and receive the Certificate of Incorporation.
required_dossiers: Notarized Memorandum and Articles of Association
Form IC-10 – Director and Officer Consent
Certified passport copy of each shareholder and director
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a query notice is issued, provide the missing attested documents within 14 days. Should the application be deemed withdrawn, file a fresh submission with the corrected record.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Appoint Registered Agent and Registered Office
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: SIFSA-licensed registered agent; Registrar for acceptance of notices
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Appoint a SIFSA-licensed agent to maintain the registered office in Samoa. Execute the registered office service agreement and file Form IC-7 with SIFSA to record the office address and agent details.
required_dossiers: Form IC-7 – Notice of Registered Office and Registered Agent
Copy of current SIFSA license of the registered agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the appointed agent cannot act or consent is withdrawn, appoint another SIFSA-licensed agent and file a replacement Form IC-7 without delay.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Adoption of First Board Resolution and Opening of Corporate Records
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Board of Directors; minutes maintained by the registered agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Convene a first board meeting, physically or by telephone/electronic means, to adopt the pro-forma resolutions approving share subscription, registered office, officer appointments and banking authorities. Maintain executed minutes and resolutions in the statutory corporate records book.
required_dossiers: Consent to act of each officer
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the meeting is procedurally defective, reconvene and adopt a ratifying resolution confirming all prior decisions.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Obtain Tax Exemption Status and Certificate of Good Standing
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registrar of International Companies, SIFSA; Ministry of Revenue for information
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Apply for the statutory international company tax exemption under the International Companies Act 1987, s. 95, and simultaneously request a Certificate of Good Standing from SIFSA evidencing current registration and no outstanding annual declarations.
required_dossiers: Certificate of Good Standing request form
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the tax exemption certificate is withheld due to an outstanding annual return, file the return and pay any penalty at the Registry before re-issuance.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Ministry of Transport and Infrastructure, Maritime, Shipping and Ports Division (Samoa)
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Shipping License and Certificate of Samoa Ship Registry under the Shipping Act 1996 (Samoa)

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministry of Natural Resources and Environment (MNRE), Samoa
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt – offshore Ro-Ro vessel operations without onshore facilities; no full EIA or environmental registration required
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Vessels must comply with MARPOL Annex I, IV, V and VI; IMO global sulphur cap of 0.50% m/m; ballast water management per the Ballast Water Management Convention; zero discharge of untreated sewage, oily bilge water, or solid waste in Samoan prohibited zones.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: International Tonnage Certificate, SOLAS Safety Certificate, International Load Line Certificate, ISPS Code Ship Security Certificate, STCW crew certification, and Samoa maritime labour compliance certificates.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Ministry for Revenue, Government of Samoa; online taxpayer portal: https://www.revenue.gov.ws
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign entity seeking a Samoa International Company tax identity must appoint a licensed registered agent and file the International Company incorporation certificate, registered agent consent, director and shareholder details, and a TIN application with the Ministry for Revenue. The Ministry issues a Tax Identification Number (TIN) within 5 business days. For VAGST, separate registration is required if taxable supplies exceed the threshold or for voluntary registration; the applicant submits a VAGST registration form, evidence of business activity, and bank account details.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Under the International Companies Act 1987, an International Company is exempt from Samoa domestic income tax and capital gains tax, provided it does not carry on business in Samoa other than offshore business. An IC may elect to be treated as an ordinary local company under the Companies Act 2001, thereby becoming subject to Samoa corporate income tax on worldwide income; alternatively, it may elect to maintain tax-exempt status by adhering to the annual licence fee filing and limitation on local-source activities. Samoa has not adopted check-the-box or hybrid mismatch elections; entity classification follows the statutory International Company regime.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: VAGST (Value Added Goods and Services Tax)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: WST 100,000 (SAT 100,000) annual taxable turnover of goods or services supplied in Samoa
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Samoa does not currently operate a mandatory real-time e-invoicing fiscal clearance system. VAGST-registered taxpayers must issue tax invoices containing prescribed particulars, retain electronic or paper records, and file periodic VAGST returns through the Ministry for Revenue e-services portal. No digital stamping or API clearance is required.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero rating applies to goods exported from Samoa within 30 days of the date of supply, to international transport services directly related to goods carried from Samoa to a destination outside Samoa (including deep-sea RoRo vehicle transport), and to services supplied directly for or in connection with exported goods. The supplier must retain documentary evidence proving export and must not be a registered person in Samoa making local consumption. Repair and maintenance of ships used in international traffic also qualify where the customer is a non-resident.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (approved by Samoa Customs Service)
Bill of Lading (signed by the ocean carrier or carrier's agent evidencing carriage of vehicles to a foreign port)
Inward Remittance Certificate (or bank SWIFT MT103 showing foreign currency credit of the export sale proceeds)
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The Ministry for Revenue may audit zero-rated export claims and require full substantiation at any time within 5 years after the taxable period. For fraudulent or unsupported zero-rating claims, Samoa law imposes a shortfall penalty of 150% of the unpaid VAGST plus interest at the prescribed late payment rate, civil penalties up to WST 100,000, retrospective clawback of the VAT input credits claimed in connection with the export, and criminal sanctions including imprisonment of up to 3 years for tax evasion or falsifying documents. Customs undervaluation or misdeclaration penalties also apply under the Customs Management Act 2014.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Central Bank of Samoa (CBS), Foreign Exchange and Banking Supervision Department; Samoa International Financial Services Authority (SIFA) as the licensing authority for International Companies
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The Samoan tala (WST) is not a freely internationally convertible currency. The CBS administers a regulated exchange-control regime under the Exchange Control Act; current-account payments are convertible through authorised dealers for genuine trade and operating expenses. Capital-account inflows into an International Company are generally exempt from CBS prior approval when the shareholder is non-resident and the proceeds are credited to a designated foreign-currency account. Profit remittances and dividend distributions to non-resident members are permitted without exchange-control restriction once the International Company confirms its exempt status under the International Companies Act, and no Samoan tax or withholding obligation attaches to such distributions. Local WST conversion is reserved for authorised-dealer transactions and should be limited to actual Samoan operating needs to avoid unnecessary convertibility friction.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: For a resident Samoan exporter, the statutory rule is repatriation of foreign-currency export proceeds within 30 days and mandatory conversion of 100% of such proceeds into WST through an authorised dealer unless a CBS exemption is obtained. For a non-resident-owned International Company engaged in RORO vehicle transport, freight revenue earned outside Samoa is treated as offshore foreign-currency income and is not subject to the resident surrender regime. Where voyage or freight receipts are collected in a Samoa bank account, the compliant structure is to maintain a CBS-approved Foreign Currency Account and apply for a general or specific exchange-control exemption so that the mandatory WST conversion ratio does not apply. Any local disbursement requiring WST should be funded through a controlled conversion executed by the authorised dealer, documented by the underlying invoice and board resolution.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow Account / Foreign-Currency Operational Account
Capital Escrow Account / Foreign-Currency Operational Account

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating is Low as a primary treasury rail and Medium only as an ancillary collection channel. An offshore digital EMI that is neither licensed nor supervised by the CBS cannot lawfully maintain a Samoa operating account, act as capital escrow custodian, or open a documentary letter of credit. A foreign EMI authorised in a reputable jurisdiction may be used to collect freight receivables and route funds by SWIFT to the Samoan bank, but it cannot replace the underlying CBS-licensed banking relationship. The EMI must apply equivalent AML/KYC diligence, verify the International Company charter and UBO structure, and all onward payments must be made to the named operational or escrow account at an authorised dealer.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Samoan banks require the International Company to be introduced by a SIFA-licensed corporate services provider registered in Apia. The registered agent and at least one authorised local signatory are normally required to attend the bank onboarding session physically. Non-resident directors and beneficial owners may accept a recorded videoconference interview if the SIFA agent is present, the documents are notarised or apostilled, and the bank's compliance officer approves the remote identification. Fully remote account opening with no Samoan nexus and no locally identifiable agent is not generally available. The bank may require physical attendance of the ultimate beneficial owner if source-of-wealth explanations are unclear or the shareholder sits in a higher-risk jurisdiction.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Bearer-share style opacity, nominee directors, or a trust structure that conceals the ultimate beneficial owner.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified International Company charter and certificate of incorporation, certificate of good standing, register of members, register of beneficial owners, full trust deed or written shareholder disclosure, notarised director identification, SIFA-licensed agent introduction letter, and board resolution designating authorised signatories.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Source of funds arising from shareholders resident in currency-control or high-risk jurisdictions, such as mainland China or Hong Kong.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Notarised corporate business licence, audited financial statements of the investing shareholder, source-of-wealth declaration, six months of bank statements from the remitting account, share subscription agreement, board resolutions for share issuance, and a payment instruction confirming that the remitter is the shareholder of record or a named third-party financier under an express escrow agreement.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Lack of commercial substance or mismatch between projected RORO shipping revenue and requested transaction value.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Detailed shipping business plan, signed voyage charters or slot-charter agreements, vessel registration and flag documents, ISM and ISPS certificates, classification certificates, P&I insurance cover, port and bunker cost projections, ship-management agreements, local substance documentation, and an organisational chart showing the International Company's operational role.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sanctions, restrictive-party, or high-risk flag exposure linked to charterers, cargo interests, vessel managers, or beneficial owners.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Independently generated sanctions-screening report for all material counterparties, charterparty and bill of lading copies, vessel ownership and flag documentation, P&I Club confirmation, goods and cargo declarations, full commercial invoice chain, and a written compliance attestation from the ship manager confirming that no prohibited country, entity, or individual is involved.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Equity and shareholder-loan injections must be routed over secure SWIFT MT103 or MT202 payment instructions to a designated USD or EUR account maintained at ANZ Samoa Limited or Bank of South Pacific (Samoa) Ltd. The remittance field must state the purpose as 'Shareholder capital injection for Samoa International Company RORO shipping operations' and, where used, an IMF BPM6/FDI purpose code accepted by the correspondent bank. The remitter must be the shareholder of record or an expressly authorised third-party lender under a written facility agreement. Before funds are applied, the receiving bank must verify the International Company certificate, authorised signatories, UBO register, and the capital-escrow release conditions. CBS exchange-control approval is not required for non-resident capital credited to a foreign-currency account of an offshore International Company; however, the bank must distinguish equity from shareholder loan and maintain the matching share subscription or loan agreement for audit trail purposes.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: RORO operating disbursements should be executed through the CBS-licensed authorised dealer using SWIFT MT103 for high-value counterparty payments to bunker suppliers, port agents, stevedores, vessel managers, crew-pay processors, insurers, and freight brokers. Commercial letters of credit are used via SWIFT MT700/MT760 for vessel-acquisition or charter-related collateral obligations and for standby guarantees required by charterers or sellers. USD payments clear through the correspondent bank's Fedwire or CHIPS access; EUR payments clear through TARGET2 via the Samoan bank's European correspondents; WST local payments settle through the Samoa domestic clearing system. Each outward MT103 must carry the exact beneficiary legal name, BIC/IBAN or account number, a reference to the underlying charterparty, port-Tariff invoice or management agreement, and a matching board-approved disbursement instruction. The operational foreign-currency account should never be used for capital-escrow release without a separate board resolution and compliance sign-off.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Forward foreign-exchange contracts in USD/EUR and USD/WST entered into with a CBS-licensed authorised dealer against documented freight, charter, bunker, or voyage-cost exposure

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) for non-deliverable cross-currency pairs such as USD/CNY or USD/JPY, transacted with a creditworthy offshore bank and supported by an underlying vessel, trade, or financing exposure
Cross-currency swaps and parallel loans used in ship-finance or asset-backed facilities to align USD debt service with EUR or JPY revenue streams

Currency and interest-rate hedging instruments embedded in an International Company banking facility where such derivatives are classified as permissible by the Samoan financial institution and approved by the board

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Government License (Registration Renewal) Fee – Samoa International Company (base rate for standard authorized capital)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registrar of International Companies, Samoa International Companies and Trusts Registry, Ministry of Commerce, Industry and Labour (Apia, Samoa)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually on the incorporation anniversary; registered agent remits the fee on the due date; 30-day grace period before late penalties accrue
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late penalty of 10% of the unpaid annual fee; if the fee remains unpaid for 3 consecutive months, the Registrar may, upon Gazetted notice, administratively strike the company off the International Companies Register, resulting in dissolution and vesting of its assets in the State

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Beneficial Ownership (UBO) Confirmation and Register Update
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Licensed Registered Agent in Samoa (maintaining the confidential beneficial ownership register); register available for lawful inspection by the Registrar and the Samoa Financial Intelligence Unit
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually on the incorporation anniversary; any change in beneficial ownership (e.g., transfer of shares in the RoRo operating holding entity) must be notified to the registered agent within 14 days of the change
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Non-compliance constitutes an offence under the International Companies (Amendment) Act 2019, attracting daily default fines and, upon conviction, statutory fines and/or imprisonment for directors; persistent breach may trigger Registrar-initiated strike-off

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: No compulsory audit for a standard Samoa International Company; audit is required only where the articles of association mandate it or where shareholders holding at least 10% of the issued shares serve a written audit demand
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: IFRS as issued by the IASB (preferred); US GAAP is also acceptable for internal statutory accounting records. The International Company must keep proper books of account recording income, expenditure, assets, liabilities and vessel-related transactions, but no financial statements are filed with the Registrar

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The International Companies (Amendment) Act 2019 requires every International Company to confirm its beneficial ownership schedule annually on the incorporation anniversary; shareholding changes (including transfers of shares in the RoRo vehicle-carrier owning entity) must be advised to the registered agent within 14 days, with simultaneous updating of the confidential UBO register
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Directors (including secretary and alternate directors)
Register of Members (maintained where the company has two or more members; single-member International Company is exempt)
Register of Charges and Mortgages (including ship mortgages over RoRo vessels)
Minute Book (recording directors' and members' resolutions)
Confidential Register of Beneficial Owners (UBO register held by the licensed registered agent)

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 750 – USD 1,500 per annum (licensed registered agent and registered office retainer)
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: Not applicable – statutory audit exemption; voluntary certified audit USD 6,000 – USD 18,000 depending on fleet size and chartering structure

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 0% for Samoa International Company; 25% standard domestic corporate rate for resident companies
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Full statutory exemption from Samoa income tax, stamp duty, and exchange control under Section 206 of the International Companies Act 1987; tax-exempt zone classification; no Samoan capital gains or social security levy on the International Company.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Not applicable — International Company does not file Samoa corporate income tax return; annual compliance is completed through the International Companies annual return lodged with the Samoa International Financial Services Centre (SIFSC) / Registrar of International Companies e-portal.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual registrar return; no quarterly or annual income tax return filing for an exempt International Company.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Registrar annual return due within 90 days after the anniversary of incorporation; the fiscal year-end may be selected freely but must be declared in the return.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Company name, International Company registration number, registered agent details, and incorporation date.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident shareholder and director must provide full legal name, passport number, residential address, and registered agent service address in Samoa.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Registered office and principal place of business in Samoa.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Must be the licensed registered office address supplied by the Samoan registered agent; no foreign street address may be substituted.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Declaration of no local taxable activity and confirmation of international company exemption eligibility.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Confirm the vessel transport activity is conducted outside Samoan territorial waters and income is not derived from a Samoan source.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late lodgement triggers default fines under the International Companies Act 1987; the Registrar may strike off and dissolve the company after three years of default; directors may be disqualified and subject to daily surcharges of WST 50 plus fines up to WST 500 per omitted return.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 0% for dividends paid by an International Company to non-resident shareholders; statutory dividend withholding tax otherwise applies at 15% for resident-company dividends but is overridden by the International Companies exemption.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Samoa does not maintain a comprehensive double tax agreement network applicable to International Companies; a non-resident shareholder may rely on the statutory exemption under the International Companies Act 1987. Where a treaty or reciprocal arrangement applies, the shareholder must file Form WHT-REL with the Samoa Ministry of Revenue before the payment date, attaching a Tax Residency Certificate (TRC) issued by the shareholder's tax authority and supporting ownership confirmation from the company's registered agent.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: 0% for an International Company paying royalty or interest to non-residents under the International Companies exemption; otherwise Samoa statutory withholding tax is 15% for interest and 15% for royalties, with treaty-negotiated rates applicable only where a relevant DTA is in force.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: No formal Samoan transfer pricing threshold for exempt International Companies; a transfer pricing documentation set, including Local File and Master File, is prudent where gross transactions with related parties exceed WST 1,000,000 or where the company materially shifts profits through charter hire arrangements.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Economic Substance Regulations (ESR) apply to Samoa International Companies carrying on relevant activities, with deep-sea Ro-Ro vehicle transport classified as a relevant activity. The company must be managed and controlled in Samoa, maintain adequate physical premises, employ competent local staff, and incur sufficient operating expenditure; an annual ESR notification and substance report must be submitted to the Samoa Registrar of International Companies.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Tax Evasion by Abusing International Company Exemption
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using an International Company to shelter income from Ro-Ro vessel transport that is effectively Samoan-source, or failing to disclose management and control exercised from Samoa.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Penalty of up to 150% of unpaid Samoan tax; default interest at 5% above government lending rates; criminal fine up to WST 50,000; confiscation of revenues attributable to the Samoan-source shipping leg.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who sign false declarations are personally liable for the unpaid tax; travel bans may be imposed; management disqualification for up to 10 years; imprisonment for up to 7 years for tax fraud.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company / Failure of Economic Substance
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Maintaining an International Company with no real commercial substance in Samoa, including absence of Samoan management decision-making, no physical office, and no locally retained records, while deriving worldwide Ro-Ro shipping profits.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Fine up to WST 250,000 for failing the economic substance test; annual penalty up to WST 50,000 for non-compliance; Registrar may strike off the company and exchange information with foreign tax authorities.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and beneficial owners may be jointly liable for the corporate fine; disgorgement of profits; travel restrictions; director disqualification for up to 5 years; imprisonment up to 3 years for submitting false substance information.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Processing Swift LC and wire transfer payments for Ro-Ro cargo services without conducting client due diligence, or routing charter payments through or to a sanctioned jurisdiction, vessel, or beneficial owner.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Entity fines up to WST 2,000,000 under Samoa AML/CFT laws; freezing orders on bank accounts; revocation of the International Company license and termination of the registered agent arrangement.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors face personal fines up to WST 1,000,000; confiscation of personal assets; travel bans during investigation; imprisonment up to 14 years for money laundering.
